subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own pace-aware provider usage policy for autonomous agents, and should the first scope be read-only visibility or opt-in throttling?
rationale: The proposal changes provider-specific usage semantics, agents.defaults config, persisted runtime state, and autonomous/subagent execution policy, so source inspection alone cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Read-only core visibility first
options.body: Normalize provider usage pace context into existing usage, status, and session_status surfaces while deferring enforcement until the data model proves reliable.

options.title: Opt-in core throttling
options.body: Add disabled-by-default pace thresholds that can throttle subagents or non-interactive work, with explicit config, tests, docs, and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Plugin/API design first
options.body: Keep core lean by exposing any missing provider usage hooks and letting a plugin or ClawHub package own pace policy.

recommendation.title: Read-only core visibility first
recommendation.body: Normalize provider usage pace context into existing usage, status, and session_status surfaces while deferring enforcement until the data model proves reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: The local history points to steipete for the current provider usage/status/auth-profile surfaces that the decision would extend.
